title: Runtime contract broadcast and version-lock schema for model onboarding
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We need a concise, machine-readable way to advertise a model's runtime contract (what it supports, its recommended operating limits, and how version-locking should behave) to the serving and routing layers and to downstream customers. Current model manifests surface capabilities in several ad-hoc fields which makes automated routing, fallback, and cost-aware decisions brittle.

Objective: Define and publish a single 'runtime_contract' envelope in the model onboarding API that exposes: 1) explicit soft and hard resource/behavior limits (max_context_tokens, tokens_per_second, kv_cache_bytes), 2) supported features (structured_output, function_calling, streaming), 3) recommended serving profile (batching_hint, quantization_profile), and 4) a version_locking policy that defines which fields are candidates for safe runtime substitution vs. those that require explicit customer approval. This ticket is the schema design + server-side publishing + console surface for preview.

Out of scope: model training metadata, in-depth UI changes to the Console beyond a preview panel, and on-prem upgrade tooling (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria: A JSON schema named runtime_contract published in the model onboarding API v2 with a stable v1beta contract ID.
Schema sections include: service_contract_id, supported_features, soft_limits, hard_limits, recommended_profile, version_lock_policy, telemetry_hints.
Serving runtime can consume the new field and make routing decisions using batch/latency hints in an internal integration test (see PR link).
Backward compatibility: existing manifests without runtime_contract must continue to be accepted; runtime will apply conservative defaults documented in the schema.
Console can display a read-only preview of the runtime_contract for newly onboarded models and surface any fields that require customer approval for version changes.
Security sign-off completed (KMS access patterns unchanged) and performance tests demonstrate no >3% added latency when the field is present.
Integration test created that validates version_lock_policy prevents automatic substitution for fields marked 'requires_approval'.
work_notes: 2025-02-16: Kickoff - scoped to schema + API surface; design sync with Console scheduled.
2025-02-17: Spike - enumerated candidate fields from runtime telemetry (kv cache, batch size, qconfig). Saved findings to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runtime+Contract+Spike
2025-02-19: Decision - use 'soft_limits' (advisory) vs 'hard_limits' (enforced) rather than single limit field to allow seamless rollouts and graceful degradation.

2025-02-21: Trade-off - embedding quantization_profile as recommendation only to avoid coupling model manifest to binary artifacts. Chosen because it simplifies pinning logic for hosted vs private deployments.
2025-02-23: API draft posted: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821. Seeking eng + PM review.
2025-02-24: Ravi - started server impl for publishing on model create/update; plan to add feature-flag gate 'enable_runtime_contract_broadcast' for 2-week canary.
2025-02-25: Design feedback from SRE - add telemetry_hints.top_k_replay and a throttle_signals section to help autoscaler make admission decisions.
2025-02-27: Added integration tests skeleton and a mock manifest producer to simulate missing runtime_contract cases.
Follow-ups: Console preview (PM ticket), Dedicated rollout checklist (ops runbook), and update onboarding docs for partners.
